solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Many grew old behind bars

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
aged means grew old

explanation.surface: Lots of people reached old age while in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving C (100) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Something behind bars is locked up, like a bird or beast in a cage.

clue.text: Time will be on its side

definitions.text: Time will be on its side

parts.words: Time will be on its side
parts.note: reads like a promise of eventual success, but describes a tall structure with a clock face showing the hours on its wall

explanation.definitionFit: A tower bearing a clock literally shows the time on each of its sides.

clue.text: Station of the Cross

parts.note: the Stations of the Cross are devotions on Christ's Passion; here 'station' is read as the place where the cross stood, the hill of the crucifixion

explanation.definitionFit: The hill outside Jerusalem where the crucifixion took place was the location of the Cross.

clue.text: Follow and observe for a two-hour period

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
watch means observe

explanation.surface: Tail someone and keep an eye on them for a couple of hours.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, each dog watch is one of the two short two-hour duty shifts in the early evening.

clue.text: Military assistant gives notice to project worker

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a notice
to jut is to project or stick out
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: An army aide hands a notice to someone employed on a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' and 'worker' look like a noun phrase about a job; they are a verb (stick out) and an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is an officer who assists a commanding officer with administration.

clue.text: Get a welcome run and declare

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, a hail of welcome
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Receive a warm greeting, go for a jog, and make an announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state or assert something firmly, the same as to declare it.

clue.text: Turnabouts in vessels

indicators.note: turn tells us that the letters following are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Reversals of direction happening on ships.
explanation.definitionFit: U-boats were German submarines, a kind of naval vessel.

clue.text: A film's been made out of it

definitions.text: A film's been made out of it

parts.words: A film's been made out of it
parts.note: sounds like a remark about a book adapted for the screen, but it points to the 1985 film whose title is 'Out of' plus a continent

explanation.definitionFit: The continent fills the gap in the film title Out of ___, starring Meryl Streep.

clue.text: Rent to the Royal Navy

parts.note: taken as written
RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Money paid for lodgings goes to the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment, but it is the past participle meaning ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is an old past participle of rend, so something rent has been ripped apart.

clue.text: Compel to do a favour, including thanks in return

indicators.note: including means one word takes the other into its middle

parts.note: to oblige someone is to do them a favour

indicators.note: in return says the word for thanks is read the other way round

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Force someone to help, with gratitude given back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do a favour' reads as part of the definition, but supplies the verb that holds the reversed thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: To obligate someone is to bind or force them to act, synonymous with compelling them.

clue.text: Turning a list into new form

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties and who does them

indicators.note: into is given a new form, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Reshaping a list into something different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new form' rearranges INTO to give TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotation is the act of turning around an axis.

clue.text: Great place for fresh air!

parts.note: reads like praise of some resort, but 'great' means huge: the whole open-air world beyond buildings

explanation.definitionFit: The open air outside any building is where fresh air is found, and it is the great outside.

clue.text: A professor of infinite wisdom

parts.note: seems to describe a brilliant academic, but 'professor' is one who professes, here someone who claims to understand everything

explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is a person who behaves as if they understand everything, professing boundless knowledge.

clue.text: A noted text-book

parts.note: suggests a famous textbook, but 'noted' means set to musical notes: the words of an opera, a book of text with music

explanation.definitionFit: The libretto is the text of an opera, published as a little book and set to notes.

clue.text: Unwillingly late

parts.note: reads as tardy against one's wishes, but 'late' means dead and 'unwillingly' means without having made a will

explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies intestate has died without leaving a valid will.

clue.text: Unusual term exists for those of a mind to go far in politics

definitions.text: those of a mind to go far in politics

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the next words appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd label exists for politically ambitious people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges TERM EXISTS. 'go far' suggests career success, but means holding far-out views.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremists hold radical views far from the political centre.

clue.text: 'Variable after a shower' etc

indicators.note: variable says the letters that follow can vary, appearing in a changed order

explanation.surface: A snippet of a forecaster's typical patter about the skies.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make the clue look like a fragment of broadcast patter, and it is exactly that: the whole clue both supplies the letters and illustrates the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrases like 'variable after a shower' are standard wording in a broadcast prediction of conditions.

clue.text: Regular lay preachers take it

parts.note: even means regular or uniform
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.walkthrough: 'lay preachers' looks like one phrase, but 'lay' is a song, and the definition is 'preachers take it', a service they conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening service of the Church of England, which clergy take or lead.

clue.text: Everybody present and of sound mind

definitions.meaning: the phrase taken literally: every person is here
the idiom for someone mentally sharp and sane

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both that everyone has turned up and, idiomatically, that someone is mentally alert.

clue.text: It was once a city Jane Eyre came to love

definitions.meaning: the Kent town lost its city status in 1998
the brooding master of Thornfield in Charlotte Brontë's novel, whom the heroine loves

explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town was a city until 1998, and Edward of that name is the man Jane Eyre loves.

clue.text: He composed music many dance to at home

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a hop is an informal dance
in means at home

explanation.surface: A composer whose music lots of people dance to in their houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was a Polish composer of piano music, much of it dances such as mazurkas.

clue.text: Incomplete Oriental holiday

indicators.note: incomplete says the word for Oriental loses its final letter

parts.note: eastern means Oriental

explanation.surface: An unfinished holiday in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is a Christian festival and a public holiday in many countries.

clue.text: Can and must resort to private study

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters are sorted again

explanation.surface: Tin and mustard turn to a private retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a noun or 'fall back on', but is re-sort, rearranging CAN MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private room where one can study or work undisturbed.

clue.text: Sole assistance for those travelling in the Arctic

definitions.text: Sole assistance for those travelling in the Arctic

parts.words: Sole assistance for those travelling in the Arctic
parts.note: 'sole' seems to mean only, but means the underside of the foot: something worn underfoot to help walk on drifts

explanation.definitionFit: A wide frame strapped to the boot spreads weight so one can walk on deep snow.

clue.text: Gets harder scenes to play

definitions.meaning: cement or jelly that hardens is said to do this
stage or film scenery, the settings actors perform in

explanation.definitionFit: A jelly sets when it hardens, and theatre sets are the scenery in which a play is acted.

clue.text: Mount hotly tipped when it runs

definitions.text: Mount hotly tipped when it runs

parts.words: Mount hotly tipped when it runs
parts.note: reads like a horse favoured in a race, but 'mount' is a mountain whose summit is hot and from which lava runs

explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano has a hot summit, and lava runs from it when it erupts.

clue.text: They swear or turn into drunkards

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: topers are habitual heavy drinkers

indicators.note: turn says the little word or is turned round

explanation.surface: People who curse, or else become drunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses OR to RO, which goes 'into' TOPERS. The idiom 'swear like a trooper' gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Troopers, cavalry soldiers, are proverbial for swearing, as in 'swear like a trooper'.

clue.text: Foreigner who loses it on marriage

definitions.text: Foreigner who loses it on marriage

parts.words: Foreigner who loses it on marriage
parts.note: suggests someone losing their temper at a wedding, but 'it' is a title: a young Spanish woman ceases to be called Miss when she weds

explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish title for an unmarried woman changes to Señora once she marries.

clue.text: Some horses eat grass, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to graze is to eat grass

explanation.surface: Certain horses feed in the pasture.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey is a horse's coat colour, so certain horses are called by it.
